subject: Re: Model regression after v2.4.1 deployment — next steps & rollback?
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-retail.com>; Jenny Park <jenny.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit & recommended next steps

Hi Samir / Jenny —

Thanks for the call today — appreciate the time and the clear context on the checkout assistant use cases and the edge-case refund flows. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) What we heard
- Primary goal: reduce incorrect refund suggestions and inaccurate policy references in the checkout assistant (peak traffic 3–5pm PT)
- Current latency targets: p95 < 600ms, cost objective is to keep token unit economics within Q4 commit
- Success metric: top-1 accuracy on the MAPS prompt set (customer-provided test set) + qualitative regression tests

2) Recommended model(s) to start with
- rwd-2.3-medium-quant: best cost/latency tradeoff for broad QA and templated responses
- rwd-2.4.1-high: higher-quality variant we showed in demo; better slot-filling but higher tail-latency in some sequences

3) Artifacts shared
- Acme eval report (summary + per-prompt diffs): acme_eval_report_v2.4.1.pdf (attached)
- Prompt set we ran: MAPS_prompt_set_v3.txt (attached)
- Benchmark dashboard link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-evals

4) Next steps (recommended)
- Short term: run a 1% canary of rwd-2.4.1 against production traffic for 48 hours and monitor MAPS regressions + human review flags.
- If we see regressions, rollback rwd-2.4.1 for the affected routes and pin to rwd-2.3-medium-quant, then iterate with a targeted evaluation set.
- Rishi / Engineering to provide a diff and rollback ETA if needed.

Please confirm if Acme is comfortable with the canary plan (1% for 48h) and whether you want Redwood to schedule the rollback window in advance.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

Attachment(s): acme_eval_report_v2.4.1.pdf, MAPS_prompt_set_v3.txt
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>; Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 18:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & recommended next steps

Marissa / team —

I took a closer look at the logs after the call and ran a focused diff between 2.3 (current pin) and 2.4.1 on Acme's MAPS set. Summary: there are measurable regressions in three prompt buckets tied to refund-policy references and numeric extraction (order totals). I attached the CSV with per-prompt delta (model-diff-2.3-2.4.1.csv).

Key findings: 
- ~6% drop in top-1 exact match for the refund-policy prompts (these are high business impact)
- Increase in hallucinated policy citations for ambiguous wording—seems related to a generation-sampling change in 2.4.1
- Latency: rwd-2.4.1 p95 is ~30% higher on long context sequences (not catastrophic, but affects tail-SLOs)

Given the business impact, I recommend we do the following immediately if Acme approves: 
1) Schedule a rollback of rwd-2.4.1 for the checkout-assistant route (we can do canary rollback within 1 hour of approval)
2) Pin the route to rwd-2.3-medium-quant while we investigate the regression root cause and prepare a targeted patch/update
3) Create an eval ticket to reproduce the exact failure cases and add those prompts to Acme's regression suite

I can run the rollback — ETA 45 minutes once the time window is agreed. Please see internal runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/model-rollback

— Ethan
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
ethan.park@redwood.com

Attachment(s): model-diff-2.3-2.4.1.csv
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenny Park <jenny.park@acme-retail.com>, procurement@acme-retail.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:03:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & recommended next steps

Marissa, Ethan —

Thanks for the quick analysis and for running the diffs. We started seeing user complaints this morning around inaccurate refund guidance in our US region (customers being told they qualify for refunds when they don't). This is material — it already caused a spike in CS tickets and one escalated refund reversal.

We are comfortable approving an immediate rollback for the checkout-assistant route. Prefer a fast rollback window (off-peak: 09:30–10:30 PT) if that works for Redwood. Also want the route pinned to the previous stable model (rwd-2.3-medium-quant) until we validate a fix.

Please confirm the rollback timeline and any expected customer-visible downtime or behavior changes. Also share the plan for adding the failing prompts to the regression suite so we can validate post-rollback.

— Samir
Director, Product — CX Automation | Acme Retail
samir.k@acme-retail.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-retail.com>; Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jenny Park <jenny.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & recommended next steps

Samir — thanks for the quick decision and for flagging the customer impact. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) Rollback window: Redwood will trigger a canary rollback to rwd-2.3-medium-quant on the checkout-assistant route starting 2026-11-02 09:30 PT (16:30 UTC) for a staged 1% -> 10% -> 100% promotion over 30 minutes if metrics look good. Full rollback completion target: 10:00 PT.

2) Expected customer impact: no downtime; responses will switch back to the previously pinned behavior. There will be a brief period (~5–10 minutes) of cache warming and slight rate-limiting while we scale the older variant back up. We do not expect increased latency beyond normal SLOs.

3) Pin: we will pin the route to rwd-2.3-medium-quant after rollback until Acme gives the green light to re-test 2.4.1. Pinning will be visible in the Console and via the HubSpot deal note.

4) Post-rollback validation: Ethan will run the failing MAPS prompt subset as smoke tests and add them to Acme's regression suite. Expected delivery for the updated regression suite: EOD 2026-11-03.

5) Follow-up: schedule a technical sync with Acme (engineering + product) to review diffs and remediate. Rishi / I will follow up on availability — propose Tue 2026-11-03 09:00 PT.

If that schedule works, Samir please reply with approval and any additional constraints from Procurement. Once approved, Ethan will start the rollback at the agreed time and update the thread with progress.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0148
